generation_1_hash_package_based.title: Reliable Third-Party Library Detection in Android and its Security Applications
generation_1_hash_package_based.method: 3-layer Merkle tree (Package→Class→Method). Fuzzy descriptors replace custom types with X. CHA for hierarchy analysis. Similarity score 0-1.
generation_1_hash_package_based.version_level_f1: 64% Group-1; 12.7% on adjacent versions under R8
generation_1_hash_package_based.obfuscation_coverage: RN only (100% resilient); fails PF (-75%), CFR, MI
generation_1_hash_package_based.sbom_output: Partial — version list, no standard format
generation_1_hash_package_based.cve_mapping: Manual — studied 2 CVEs (FB SDK, Dropbox SDK)

generation_1_hash_package_based.title: LibRadar: Fast and Accurate Detection of Third-Party Libraries in Android Apps
generation_1_hash_package_based.method: Android API frequency hashing + package clustering. Whitelist-based. No decompilation.
generation_1_hash_package_based.version_level_f1: None — clustering only, no version labels
generation_1_hash_package_based.obfuscation_coverage: RN, PF; fails CFR, DCR, SE, MI

generation_1_hash_package_based.title: LibD: Scalable and Precise Third-party Library Detection in Android Markets
generation_1_hash_package_based.method: Homogeny graph (call/inherit/inclusion). CFG opcode hashing per basic block → method→class→instance fingerprint.
generation_1_hash_package_based.lib_level_f1: High — 1,954 libs vs LibRadar's 670, FP 25% vs 60.6%
generation_1_hash_package_based.r8_resilience: Strong against RN, PF by design; CFR, MI untested
generation_1_hash_package_based.speed: Medium — 1.4M apps tested, no per-app timing
generation_1_hash_package_based.partial_lib: No — instance hash only, no score

generation_1_hash_package_based.title: ORLIS: Obfuscation-Resilient Library Detection for Android
generation_1_hash_package_based.method: Two-stage: sdhash app-filter → ssdeep CFG class matching + Jaccard similarity
generation_1_hash_package_based.version_level_f1: Not reported as version metric (implicit CFG fine-grained)
generation_1_hash_package_based.r8_resilience: Partial — best Gen-1 obfusc resilience; not tested on R8
generation_1_hash_package_based.obfuscation_coverage: RN, PF, CFR; SE, MI untested
generation_1_hash_package_based.open_source: Partial — published, hard to install (Soot env)

generation_2_cdg_based.title: ATVHUNTER: Reliable Version Detection of Third-Party Libraries for Vulnerability Identification in Android Applications
generation_2_cdg_based.method: CDG module decoupling → coarse CFG filter → fine opcode fuzzy rolling hash + feature weighting
generation_2_cdg_based.r8_resilience: Partial — DashO tested; 99.3% under RN+PF; -24% DCR; MI not tested
generation_2_cdg_based.module_decoupling: CDG — Class Dependency Graph (best among Gen-2)
generation_2_cdg_based.sbom_output: Partial — CVE-linked version list, no standard SBOM format
generation_2_cdg_based.open_source: Partial — online service, source partially released
generation_2_cdg_based.cve_mapping: Yes — 1,180 CVEs, 224 security bugs, 189K TPLs, 3M versions

generation_3_r8_aware.title: Obfuscation-resilient Detection of Android Third-Party Libraries Using Multi-Scale Code Dependency Fusion
generation_3_r8_aware.method: Multi-scale fusion: CDG + function call + basic block dependency. LDG. Bayesian probability scoring. Explicit SBOM generation.
generation_3_r8_aware.lib_level_f1: High — exceeds single-scale baselines (exact score unverified)
generation_3_r8_aware.version_level_f1: Strong — Bayesian scoring targets adjacent-version disambiguation
generation_3_r8_aware.r8_resilience: Strong — dependency graph stable under R8 shrinking & inlining
generation_3_r8_aware.obfuscation_coverage: RN, PF, CFR, MI — designed for R8 inlining
generation_3_r8_aware.sbom_output: Explicit SBOM — primary goal: SBOM + CVE mapping

generation_3_r8_aware.title: Android Third-Party Library Detection via Feature Language Model (LibAttention)
generation_3_r8_aware.method: Pre-train Transformer on 200M Smali tokens → fine-tune binary classifier. SDK structural vocabulary. Feature compression.
generation_3_r8_aware.r8_resilience: Best overall — +30% F1 over rule-based on R8-obf-shr-opt
generation_3_r8_aware.obfuscation_coverage: All R8 modes — RN, PF, CFR, DCR, SE, MI
generation_3_r8_aware.sbom_output: No — no version → no CVE → no SBOM
generation_3_r8_aware.open_source: Partial — code described, full release unclear

generation_3_r8_aware.title: Version-level Third-Party Library Detection in Android Applications via Class Structural Similarity (SAD)
generation_3_r8_aware.method: CDG + neighbor aggregation → stateful/stateless class split → Field Op Sequence vs opcode → literal tie-breaker
generation_3_r8_aware.r8_resilience: Strong for RN, PF, CFR, DCR; -10pp under heavy inlining (MI)
generation_3_r8_aware.obfuscation_coverage: RN, PF, CFR, DCR; weaker on MI
generation_3_r8_aware.sbom_output: Partial — version labels, no CVE mapping
generation_3_r8_aware.open_source: Partial — EASE 2025; availability unclear at submission

generation_3_r8_aware.title: Towards Global Matches for Third-Party Library Detection in Android
generation_3_r8_aware.method: Bloom filter feature abstraction + back-and-forth iterative global matching elevating pairwise to set-level similarity
generation_3_r8_aware.key_results: Outperforms SOTA on two public benchmarks. Addresses local-maxima problem. Open source on Zenodo.
generation_3_r8_aware.partial_lib: Set-level similarity handles partial inclusion implicitly
weaknesses: Specific numeric results pending full publication

generation_3_r8_aware.title: Libra: Library Identification in Obfuscated Android Apps
generation_3_r8_aware.method: Two-phase: method headers (coarse) → CTPH piecewise fuzzy hashing (fine). Compact instruction encoding.
generation_3_r8_aware.key_results: F1 88% non-obfuscated, 50-87% obfuscated. Outperforms prior work.
generation_3_r8_aware.partial_lib: CTPH fuzzy matching handles partial code
strengths: CTPH piecewise fuzzy hashing robust to reordering

generation_3_r8_aware.title: LibScan / LibHunter (Wu+ 2023)
generation_3_r8_aware.method: Opcode + call chain similarity. LibHunter extends with method inlining simulation and call-site optimization handling.

generation_3_r8_aware.title: LibPecker (Zhan+ 2020)
generation_3_r8_aware.method: Class dependency hashing + adaptive class similarity thresholds + weighted class similarity
generation_3_r8_aware.obfuscation_coverage: Best Gen-1 against obfuscation (per Zhan ASE 2020)
strengths: Best precision-recall trade-off on real-world dataset
weaknesses: Per TPL-Benchmark, peak F1 is 60.15% — much lower than originally claimed

surveys_and_benchmarks.title: A Systematic Assessment on Android Third-party Library Detection Tools
key_findings: Richer features (class deps) = better obfuscation resilience
Multidex is a critical blind spot (-50% recall)
Tools fail on partial import TPLs, obfuscated TPLs, TPL dependency
No tool handles all cases — hybrid approaches needed

surveys_and_benchmarks.title: Revisiting Third-Party Library Detection: A Ground Truth Dataset and Its Implications Across Security Tasks
surveys_and_benchmarks.dataset: 6,055 apps, 5,756 unique TPLs, 15,274 versions, 62,218 App-TPL mappings
key_findings: Highest library-level F1 = 60.15% (LibPecker) — much lower than prior claims (83-97%)
Over half of apps use R8 compiler
728 libraries with ≥1 CVE, 3,309 TPL-CVE pairs, 8,115 App-CVE mappings
R8 shrinks >50% cause sharp recall drops

surveys_and_benchmarks.title: An Empirical Study on the Robustness of Android TPL Detection Tools Against Advanced Obfuscation
key_findings: F1 <50% library-level, <10% version-level under advanced obfuscation
Identifies package hierarchy obfuscation as critical blind spot
Systematic failure analysis of existing tools

surveys_and_benchmarks.title: Empirical Study of Third-Party Library Detection in iOS and Android Applications
key_findings: iOS detection is ~10 years behind Android
iOS has zero version identification capability
Symbol stripping drops iOS detection to 0%

surveys_and_benchmarks.title: UniBOM — A Unified SBOM Analysis and Visualisation Tool for IoT Systems and Beyond
surveys_and_benchmarks.method: Multi-modal SBOM: binary + filesystem + source code analysis. AI-based CVE classification. Historical CPE tracking.
surveys_and_benchmarks.relevance: Architectural template for SBOM pipeline. Not Android-specific but transferable design patterns.

research_gaps.detail: Even SAD loses -10pp under heavy inlining. Most tools ignore it entirely. R8 inlining fundamentally changes code structure.
Only LibMD (unreleased) generates structured SBOM. All other tools output informal results (lib names, version lists, class mappings).
Best is 84.82% (SAD) — but this drops below 10% under advanced obfuscation (ObfDetector study). Not reliable for production.
~47.3% of TPLs depend on others. Only LibMD's LDG concept addresses this. Most tools assume flat library structure.
TPL-Benchmark (2025) shows realistic F1 is ~60% at library level, not 83-97% as prior papers claimed. Evaluation on easy datasets inflates numbers.
Most tools produce binary yes/no. Few (ORLIS, ATVHUNTER, SAD) handle partial inclusion but with limited scoring.
ObfDetector (ICSE 2026) identifies this as a critical blind spot that most tools ignore.
